applies_when: The product or its immediate shelf area occupies a visually prominent shopper-facing position and has visible space that could support communication.
check: Is the product presentation using its visible shopper-facing space effectively for branding, benefits, navigation, or promotional communication beyond the package itself?
suggestion: Strengthen the presentation with an appropriately scaled communication element such as shelf signage, a graphic panel, shelf-edge treatment, riser, or other branded component when the visible fixture and available space support it.
physical_requirements: space sufficient for a communication element
do_not_suggest_when: the area is already visually saturated
the visible surface belongs to another product or brand
there is no physically plausible communication surface

applies_when: The product is presented on a shelf, tray, rack, or small fixture and unused vertical space is visibly available above the merchandise.
check: Would a riser or other raised communication element improve visibility, brand presence, shopper navigation, or product understanding without obstructing the merchandise?
suggestion: Consider a riser, low header, or raised branded communication element when the visible fixture geometry and vertical clearance support it.
do_not_suggest_when: the vertical area is occupied by another fixture
a riser would obstruct product visibility
the scene does not establish usable vertical clearance

applies_when: A launch, limited-time item, line extension, promotional product, or concentrated product grouping is visibly present and a shelf-level dedicated presentation could plausibly support it.
check: Would a PDQ, tray, or compact dedicated display create a stronger shelf-level destination and improve organization, branding, or launch visibility?
suggestion: Use a PDQ, branded tray, counter display, or compact shelf display when product size, quantity, shelf surface, and promotional context visibly support a dedicated shelf-level presentation.
physical_requirements: product size compatible with a compact fixture
do_not_suggest_when: only large floor merchandise is visible
there is no usable shelf or counter footprint
the scene is clearly better suited to a large secondary display

applies_when: The visible package geometry appears stable and repeatable enough to support stacking or tiered presentation.
check: Could stacking or tiering improve product density, visibility, organization, or use of vertical space without creating instability?
suggestion: Consider a stacked, stepped, or tiered presentation when the package geometry, visible clearance, and available merchandising footprint support it.
do_not_suggest_when: package geometry appears unstable
vertical clearance is insufficient
stacking would obstruct branding or shopper access

applies_when: The selected product is visibly adjacent to another product category and the relationship is supported by packaging, signage, provided context, or an obvious shared use case.
check: Could a compact physical merchandising element create a clearer and more intentional connection between the adjacent categories?
suggestion: Where the relationship is visually supported, consider a PDQ, tray, shelf-edge element, divider, or small cross-merchandising fixture that connects the categories without disrupting the primary shelf.
do_not_suggest_when: the relationship between products is speculative
the categories are not visibly connected
the physical area cannot support a shared element

applies_when: Multiple visible brand, product, campaign, promotional, or fixture communication elements appear around the selected product.
check: Do the visible physical and digital communication elements read as one coordinated branded experience?
suggestion: Align messaging, graphics, benefit callouts, fixture treatments, and product presentation so the shopper experiences one clear visual hierarchy and brand story.
do_not_suggest_when: only one communication element is visible
the apparent inconsistency cannot be established from the image

applies_when: Packaging, signage, a display, or another shopper-facing communication surface is visible and additional information could reasonably improve the shopper experience.
check: Could a digital bridge provide useful education, product details, demonstrations, comparison content, or campaign continuation?
suggestion: Consider a QR code or other digital bridge only when the visible product or communication context suggests shoppers would benefit from additional information beyond what the physical execution can communicate.
do_not_suggest_when: a digital bridge would add no clear shopper value
there is no usable communication surface
the recommendation would be generic rather than scene-specific

applies_when: Visible shelf, tray, or pegboard space exists around the selected product and the current use of that existing merchandising footprint can be evaluated.
check: Is the product using its current visible shelf, tray, or pegboard allocation effectively, or are meaningful gaps, weak facings, underfilled zones, or poorly used areas reducing the strength of the presentation?
suggestion: Improve facings, blocking, placement, density, or use of the existing merchandising footprint. Consider a tray, divider, riser, rack, or shelf communication element only when the visible space and product geometry support a stronger physical solution.
visual_signals: small product block within a larger available area
do_not_suggest_when: the image does not establish ownership of the open space
the gap may clearly belong to another product
additional product or fixture would obstruct shopper access

applies_when: A sample, tester, trial-size, demonstration, or sampling presentation is visibly present.
check: Does the sampling presentation clearly connect the interaction to the brand, product, benefit, or purchase path?
suggestion: Strengthen the sampling presentation with a branded header, callout panel, riser, instruction element, or other communication that connects the trial experience to the product.
do_not_suggest_when: no sample or tester is visible

applies_when: The selected product has visible shelf-edge, price-rail, or adjacent horizontal communication space.
check: Is the shelf edge being used effectively for branding, product differentiation, navigation, benefits, or promotional communication?
suggestion: Use shelf-edge signage, strips, blades, callouts, price-rail graphics, or other compact branded elements when they can add useful communication without requiring a larger fixture.
visual_signals: product directly above usable shelf edge
do_not_suggest_when: the shelf edge is occupied by required retailer labeling
there is no usable shelf-edge surface

applies_when: A fixture or product grouping has visible structural or vertical space above it that could plausibly support a header, topper, or raised communication element.
check: Would a header or topper create a stronger branded destination, campaign connection, product navigation, or shopper-facing hierarchy?
suggestion: Add or strengthen a header, topper, or riser only when the visible structure and available vertical space physically support it.
do_not_suggest_when: only ordinary open air above an inline shelf is visible
there is no plausible mounting or structural support
the header would obstruct another fixture

applies_when: A dedicated display, rack, fixture, or merchandising structure has a clearly visible side surface exposed to shopper traffic.
check: Is the visible side surface being used effectively for branding, benefits, education, campaign continuation, or navigation?
suggestion: Use available side-panel surfaces for branded graphics, benefit communication, campaign continuation, or supporting shopper messaging when the side is visibly exposed.
physical_requirements: visible side panel or structural side surface
do_not_suggest_when: the side surface is not shopper-visible
no meaningful side panel exists

applies_when: Meaningful unused height is visibly available within or immediately above the selected product's current merchandising footprint.
check: Could the unused height within the current merchandising area support additional product, tiering, stacking, signage, a riser, header, or another appropriately scaled structure?
suggestion: Use clearly available vertical capacity within the current merchandising footprint for additional product presentation or branded communication when package geometry, fixture structure, shopper access, and visible clearance support it.
do_not_suggest_when: the open area clearly belongs to another fixture
the vertical space cannot safely support additional merchandising
the image does not establish sufficient clearance
ordinary open air above an inline shelf is not evidence of usable vertical merchandising space

applies_when: The selected product is merchandised on standard retail infrastructure and visible evidence supports moving beyond a modest shelf-level enhancement to a truly dedicated branded merchandising structure.
check: Would a dedicated merchandising structure materially improve organization, capacity, visibility, branding, campaign communication, or shopper navigation beyond what a tray, divider, riser, or other modest shelf-level enhancement could reasonably accomplish?
suggestion: Recommend the smallest meaningful dedicated display format supported by the visible environment. Use a PDQ or compact dedicated fixture for shelf-level needs; use racks or side-oriented structures only where their placement is supported; and reserve endcap, floorstand, or pallet-scale recommendations for scenes that visibly establish those contexts.
physical_requirements: enough visible product or assortment to justify a dedicated presentation
visible footprint compatible with the proposed format
do_not_suggest_when: the proposed display scale is not supported by visible space
an aisle-end location is not visible but an endcap is being considered
floor space is not visible but a floorstand is being considered
product volume is too small for the proposed format
a modest shelf-level enhancement would adequately solve the visible condition

applies_when: A sidekick, sidecap, endcap, floorstand, pallet display, rack, or similarly substantial dedicated structure is visibly present.
check: Are the front, side, header, shelf, and structural surfaces working together effectively for product presentation and communication?
suggestion: Use the available display surfaces as a coordinated system for branding, messaging, shopper navigation, product hierarchy, and campaign communication rather than treating each surface independently.
do_not_suggest_when: the identified surface is not shopper-visible
the display is already fully utilized

applies_when: A dedicated display fixture has visible product capacity or merchandising zones.
check: Is the available display capacity being used intentionally, or does the fixture appear meaningfully underfilled, poorly organized, or structurally mismatched to the merchandise?
suggestion: Improve product quantity, facings, shelf configuration, stacking, tray layout, or product flow. If the underfill appears structural rather than temporary, consider resizing or reconfiguring the fixture.
physical_requirements: existing dedicated fixture with visible capacity
do_not_suggest_when: the image cannot distinguish temporary sell-down from structural underutilization

applies_when: A sidekick, sidecap, endcap, floorstand, pallet display, or other secondary merchandising placement is visibly present.
check: Does the secondary display create a distinct branded destination and justify its additional retail footprint?
suggestion: Strengthen the secondary display through clearer hierarchy, dedicated messaging, better product organization, stronger campaign integration, or a more intentional structural treatment.
do_not_suggest_when: the scene does not establish a secondary placement

applies_when: Part of the selected product, package face, branding, or product communication is visibly blocked or difficult to see.
check: Is the primary product face or communication obscured by adjacent products, shelf hardware, signage, fixture components, or poor placement?
suggestion: Correct the obstruction. If the obstruction appears structural or recurring, consider a tray, divider, shelf-management component, fixture adjustment, or redesigned merchandising element that preserves product visibility.
do_not_suggest_when: the apparent obstruction is caused only by camera angle

applies_when: Multiple units or facings of the selected product are visible.
check: Are the visible units faced, aligned, grouped, and contained in a way that creates a clear and intentional product presentation?
suggestion: Improve facing alignment and grouping. If recurring disorder appears related to the fixture rather than simple maintenance, consider a tray, divider, rail, channel, or other product-management structure that helps maintain presentation quality.
do_not_suggest_when: only one unit is visible
the apparent disorder is caused by occlusion or camera angle

applies_when: The selected product visually blends into surrounding merchandise or lacks a clear branded boundary from adjacent products.
check: Would structure, spacing, signage, graphics, color, product blocking, or a dedicated branded element help the selected product read as a distinct destination?
suggestion: Create stronger visual separation using the smallest meaningful combination of branded graphics, shelf structure, trays, dividers, signage, product blocking, or dedicated merchandising supported by the visible environment.
visual_signals: selected product blends with neighboring products
do_not_suggest_when: the product already has clear visual ownership
adjacent merchandise is not visible enough to compare

applies_when: Digital media, promotional graphics, launch communication, campaign signage, or other strong branded communication appears visibly near the selected product.
check: Does the physical product presentation reinforce the surrounding campaign strongly enough, or is there a visible gap between the strength of the campaign communication and the merchandise presentation?
suggestion: Where supported by the scene, connect the campaign more directly to the merchandise through a branded tray, riser, shelf-edge treatment, header, callout panel, graphic fixture element, or appropriately scaled dedicated display.
visual_signals: strong media presence with weak physical merchandising
physical_requirements: visible physical merchandise associated with the communication
do_not_suggest_when: the campaign cannot confidently be associated with the selected product
the physical presentation already fully reinforces the campaign

applies_when: Multiple SKUs, variants, sizes, flavors, colors, or product types from the selected assortment are visibly presented together.
check: Is the assortment organized into a clear visual block with understandable hierarchy, grouping, and navigation?
suggestion: Improve assortment blocking using product grouping, dividers, trays, shelf communication, variant callouts, navigation graphics, or a dedicated fixture structure when the visible assortment complexity supports it.
physical_requirements: multiple visible products within the assortment
do_not_suggest_when: only one SKU is visible
assortment relationships cannot be established

applies_when: The selected product is presented directly on standard retail infrastructure and a modest shelf-level physical component could improve organization, brand ownership, containment, navigation, or presentation quality without requiring a separate secondary placement.
check: Would adding a modest shelf-level physical component materially improve the current presentation more than a simple execution correction, without requiring a full dedicated or secondary display?
suggestion: Consider a tray, divider, channel, rail, riser, small rack, shelf frame, graphic insert, or other compact branded merchandising component when it solves a visible shelf-level condition. Do not escalate to a larger dedicated or secondary display unless the scene supports that larger scale.
physical_requirements: product scale compatible with shelf-level merchandising
do_not_suggest_when: the product already has a strong dedicated fixture
the visible opportunity clearly requires a larger secondary display
there is no usable local footprint

applies_when: The selected product or assortment presents visible complexity, differentiation, features, variants, usage cues, or purchase decisions that could reasonably benefit from clearer shopper-facing explanation.
check: Could clearer physical communication help shoppers understand product benefits, differences, usage, features, or which option is right for them?
suggestion: When the visible product complexity supports it, use benefit callouts, comparison graphics, instructional messaging, navigation, shelf communication, or fixture graphics to make the product easier to understand and shop.
physical_requirements: visible evidence of a shopper education or differentiation need
a plausible shopper-facing communication surface or fixture
do_not_suggest_when: the image does not establish a meaningful education or differentiation need
the relevant product information is too blurry or obstructed to evaluate
the existing physical presentation already communicates the needed distinctions clearly

applies_when: Existing shopper-facing graphics, signage, printed panels, headers, wraps, or other branded surfaces are visibly present and their physical condition can be evaluated.
check: Are the visible graphics or signage physically degraded, damaged, faded, peeling, dirty, poorly installed, incomplete, or otherwise weakened enough to reduce the quality of the shopper-facing presentation?
suggestion: Refresh or replace the affected shopper-facing graphic components using an appropriately scaled replacement panel, header, shelf graphic, side graphic, wrap, or retrofit graphic kit when visible physical deterioration is reducing brand impact.
visual_signals: missing or incomplete visible graphic section
physical_requirements: existing shopper-facing graphic or signage surface
visible physical condition that can be evaluated
do_not_suggest_when: apparent damage could be explained by glare, reflection, blur, or camera angle
no visible physical degradation is present
the concern depends on knowing an external compliance specification or approved artwork

applies_when: The visible retail environment establishes a plausible secondary-placement context beyond the product's primary shelf, and the visible product volume, campaign strength, assortment size, or merchandising need supports considering that additional placement.
check: Does the visible scene establish both a credible need for secondary placement and the physical context required for a specific sidekick, sidecap, endcap, floorstand, or pallet-scale solution?
suggestion: Recommend a sidekick, sidecap, endcap, floorstand, or pallet-format placement only when the scene establishes the corresponding physical context. Prefer smaller secondary formats when evidence for a larger footprint is limited.
physical_requirements: visible context supporting the proposed placement scale
do_not_suggest_when: only an inline shelf is visible and no secondary-placement context is established
an endcap is proposed without visible aisle-end evidence
a floorstand is proposed without visible floor footprint
a pallet display is proposed without sufficient volume or pallet-scale space
product or category suitability alone is not evidence that a secondary placement exists
do not infer unseen aisle-end, side-of-fixture, floor, or pallet space from an ordinary inline shelf
